naslov: The Greatness of Allah's Mercy Towards His Creatures

segmenti.tekst: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ نَحْمَدُهُ وَنَسْتَعِينُهُ وَنَسْتَغْفِرُهُ
segmenti.prevod: All praise belongs to Allah; we praise Him, seek His help and ask His forgiveness.

segmenti.tekst: وَنَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شُرُورِ أَنْفُسِنَا وَمِنْ سَيِّئَاتِ أَعْمَالِنَا مَنْ يَهْدِهِ اللَّهُ فَلَا مُضِلَّ لَهُ، وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَا هَادِيَ لَهُ
segmenti.prevod: We seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our souls and from our bad deeds. Whomever Allah guides, none can lead astray, and whomever He leaves astray, none can guide.

segmenti.tekst: وَأَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ
segmenti.prevod: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, Who has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger.

segmenti.tekst: أَرْسَلَهُ اللَّهُ بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا وَسِرَاجًا مُنِيرًا لِيُنْذِرَ مَنْ كَانَ حَيًّا وَيَحِقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ صَلَّى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ الطَّيِّبِينَ الطَّاهِرِينَ وَأَصْحَابِهِ الْكِرَامِ الْهُدَاةِ الْمُهْتَدِينَ وَسَلَّمَ تَسْلِيمًا كَثِيرًا إِلَى يَوْمِ الدِّينِ
segmenti.prevod: Allah sent him with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings, a warner and a light-giving lamp, to warn whoever is alive (of heart) and so that the Word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers (Ya-Sin 36:70). May Allah the Exalted bless him and his good and pure family and his noble companions, the rightly guided who guided others, and grant him abundant peace until the Day of Judgement.

segmenti.tekst: قَالَ اللَّهُ فِي كِتَابِهِ الْكَرِيمِ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ أَمَّا بَعْدُ
segmenti.prevod: Allah says in His noble Book: “O you who believe, fear Allah as He deserves to be feared, and do not die except as Muslims.” (Al Imran 3:102). To proceed:

segmenti.tekst: Praise belongs to Allah alone, the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, the Lord of all the worlds, the Lord of the Day of Judgement,

the Lord of jinn and mankind. May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, [unclear], upon his companions, and upon all those who follow his path until the Day of Judgement.

Amin, ya Rabbal-'alamin. After the Battle of Hunayn, a battle by which the light, the light of Islam, was supposed to be extinguished, a battle launched against the Muslims by the two largest tribes of that time, Hawazin and Thaqif,

a battle in which, after the conquest of Makkah, these two tribes came out with everything they had, with their wealth, their families, their livestock – and the Muslims, by Allah's leave, won this battle, despite the great trial that befell them at that time.

After this battle, dear brothers, since the mushrikun, the unbelievers, had brought their families with them, and many of them were killed, they left behind their families, their wives, their children.
After that, the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, ordered his companions to gather these women and these children in one place and to treat them well.
While the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, was sitting with his companions after the battle, he noticed a woman running from child to child, from mother to mother.

And whenever she came across a child, she would pick it up and look at it to see whether it was hers or not. And all of it in a hurry. In the end that mother, that woman, found her child, and she began to hug it, began to kiss it, rejoicing that she had found it. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, addressing his companions, says to them: "Do you see that mother?"

The companions say: "We see her." "Would that mother throw this child of hers into the fire?" The companions looked at the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, in astonishment, saying: "No, O Messenger of Allah! How could a mother throw her child into the fire, a mother who loves her child most and who is most merciful towards her child?"
What does the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say to them? He says: "Allah is more merciful towards His servants than this mother is towards her child." Allahu akbar, [unclear].
How the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, with a single example conveys to the companions the mercy of the Most High Lord. How with a single example he conveys the mercy of our Lord.

How disobedient we are, dear brothers, to our mothers, how many times we even offend our mothers and are disobedient. And there are also those, Allah forbid, who strike their mother. What does the mother say?
Why? Because our mother loves us the most, because she is the most merciful.

Let each person analyse his day, his life. How disobedient we are, my dear brothers, to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. How many times in a single day we overstep the limits of Allah, in disobedience to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala,

through various sins, and despite that Allah gives us health, families, gives us all His blessings, gives us wealth, despite our being disobedient and rebellious towards Him. What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say in the Qur'an: "My mercy encompasses everything", all of you. And during the day, in every rak'ah, we praise Allah with the words

Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim: the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Merciful towards all creatures, Compassionate towards His believing servants (mu'minun). What does the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say: "Lillahi mi'atu rahmatin" – he says: Allah has a hundred mercies. One of them, he says, He sent down upon jinn, humans and animals, so that through it they would treat one another well, feel compassion, so that they would be merciful to one another.

And He kept 99 mercies for the Day of Judgement, so that with them He would be merciful towards His servants. That is the mercy of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. That is the mercy of our Lord. How can a person attain the mercy of Allah? The first thing, dear brothers, is that a person asks Allah for mercy.

That a person asks Allah for mercy. Because Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says in the Qur'an, when Musa, alayhis-salam (peace be upon him), asked Him for mercy, for help. What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say? "وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ مِنْ رَحْمَتِنَا أَخَاهُ هَارُونَ نَبِيًّا" – and He says: out of Our mercy, because he asked Us, We gave him Harun.
We made Harun, his brother, a prophet, so that he would help him. And Harun helped him to the end. Allah had mercy on him and sent his brother as a prophet to be a help to him.

The second thing, how a person can attain the mercy of Allah – and here, by Allah, the beauty of this religion of ours is reflected. Pay attention, dear brothers, to this hadith. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "Ar-rahimuna yarhamuhumur-Rahman."

Those who are merciful, people who are merciful, the Most Merciful will have mercy on them, that is, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, will have mercy on them. What does the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say further? "Irhamu man fil-ard."

Be merciful towards those who are on the Earth, towards the creatures. He did not say only towards the believers and so on, but towards all: towards people, and towards animals, and so on. "Yarhamkum man fis-sama'." The One who is in the heavens will have mercy on you.
So, the rule is: be merciful towards your… towards the creatures of Allah, towards your brothers, towards animals. Be merciful, and Allah will be merciful towards you.

This, dear brothers, by no means means that a person should rely on Allah's mercy and then overstep Allah's limits, overstep Allah's limits in sinning. Because you know that a mother loves her child, but sometimes that mother also punishes that child, disciplines it.

Do not let this great mercy (rahmah) of the Lord deceive a person, because Allah is just. What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say, addressing the Prophet in the Qur'an? He says: "Inform My servants that I am the One who forgives, who is merciful." What does He say further, in the continuation? "And that My punishment…" – but also that My punishment is a painful punishment – for those who overstep My limits

which I have set for the creatures. That is why, dear brothers, let us ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, for mercy, so that He has mercy on us, so that He sets our condition right. Also, let us be merciful towards one another. That is, wallahi, so… we are very much in need of this mercy, of being merciful towards one another, of loving one another, of respecting one another, because without this mercy we will certainly not get far.
أَقُولُ قَوْلِي هَٰذَا وَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ لِي وَلَكُمْ فَاسْتَغْفِرُوهُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ
segmenti.prevod: I say these words of mine and ask Allah for forgiveness for myself and for you, so ask Him for forgiveness; truly He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
